scope: Queryable original OIP part catalog and typed parameter/signal declarations

signals.name: speedTag
signals.label: Speed tag
signals.desc: The program commands belt speed here, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0 - so a half-wired belt sits still rather than running at its authored speed.

signals.name: speedFpmTag
signals.label: Speed tag
signals.desc: The program commands surface speed here in feet per minute, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Once BOUND this takes over even if no program writes it, so an unwritten tag holds the conveyor at 0.

signals.name: runTag
signals.label: Run tag (belt runs while true)
signals.desc: Start/stop gate: false forces the speed to 0 whatever the setpoint says. Unlike the speed tag, this only takes effect once a program actually DRIVES it, so binding it alone will not stop the belt.

signals.name: runningTag
signals.label: Running tag (true while moving)
signals.desc: Feedback the belt publishes for the program to read: true whenever it is actually moving. This is the EFFECTIVE speed, gates included, so a run tag holding the belt at zero reads false here.

signals.name: velocityTag
signals.label: Velocity tag (30 at the speed above)
signals.desc: Drive feedback the program reads: the effective speed as a share of the speed at 30 revolutions, times 30. Stopped reads 0, and a run tag holding the conveyor still counts as stopped.

signals.name: pulseTag
signals.label: Pulse tag (one per pitch)
signals.desc: An encoder for the program to count: TRUE for one simulation step each time the surface has travelled the inches above, in either direction, and FALSE otherwise.

signals.name: encoderTag
signals.label: Encoder tag (travel)
signals.desc: Odometer of surface travel in metres, integrated on sim time: it climbs while the conveyor runs forward and counts back while it reverses. Latch it when a photo-eye sees a box, then act once it has advanced a known distance - the standard way to track product without a sensor at every station.

params.label: Shape preset
params.desc: One-tap template for the segment table below. Picking an option writes its rows into Segments, which stays the source of truth - so hand-editing the table afterwards drifts this back to Custom rather than fighting you.

params.label: Segments
params.desc: One row per straight run: how long it is and how steeply it climbs, with the bend between runs filleted automatically. Add rows to build an incline, a Z-frame or a walk-through. The viewport shows a dot per run, so this is usually easier to drag than to type.

params.label: Width (m)
params.desc: Belt width across the direction of travel. Drag the dot on either side face to resize in the viewport.

params.label: Frame height (m)
params.desc: Depth of the bed itself: deck down to underside, which is also the fillet radius where two segments meet and the depth of the side frame. NOT the height off the floor - that is Stand height below.

params.label: Stand height (m)
params.desc: Height of the deck above whatever is beneath it, which sets the leg length. The host fills this in when you drop or snap the conveyor, so the legs reach the floor - or a platform crossing underneath - without you measuring. Pin it by hand when you want a deliberate height.

params.label: PLC speed in FPM
params.desc: The unit the PLC commands this conveyor in. On: feet per minute. Off: metres per second. The speed tag is a REAL either way, so switching changes what its value means and never how the program declares it. Set by the scene Units (Scene Properties), which switch every conveyor together, so the Inspector does not show it. A conveyor saved before this switch existed is in metres per second.

params.label: Speed
params.desc: Surface speed in feet per minute. Negative runs it backwards. A program can command this through the FPM speed tag below.

params.label: Speed
params.desc: Surface speed carried along the bed. Negative runs the belt backwards, which is the ONLY way to reverse flow - rotating the part 180 degrees moves its ends instead. A program can command this through the speed tag below.

params.label: Accel time
params.desc: How long the drive takes to bring the conveyor from stopped up to its rated speed (the speed that reads 30, under Comms > Feedback), like the acceleration time set on a VFD. A smaller change takes proportionally less. 0 starts instantly.

params.label: Decel time
params.desc: How long the drive takes to bring the conveyor from rated speed down to a stop. Cargo keeps travelling while it does, so a box stopped at a photo-eye ends up past it. 0 stops instantly.

params.label: Friction
params.desc: Grip between the running surface and a standard carton, the figure a belt datasheet quotes. A smooth PVC belt is about 0.4, a rough-top incline belt about 0.9 and a low-friction plastic modular belt about 0.2, made for product to slide while it accumulates. Bare steel rollers are about 0.4. Other cargo grips by its own friction against the same surface.

params.label: Belt color
params.desc: Tint multiplied into the belt weave. White leaves the fabric at full brightness; a dark tint multiplies it down toward black.

params.label: Belt weave
params.desc: Which fabric the belt surface wears. Alternate carries directional arrows that scroll along travel, which is the cheapest way to make flow direction readable in a screenshot.

params.label: Frame rails
params.desc: Structural rails down both sides of the bed. Cosmetic - the running surface and its collision are unaffected.

params.label: Left guard
params.desc: Guard wall down the left side, looking along travel. This is a real barrier, so turning it off lets cargo leave the belt sideways.

params.label: Right guard
params.desc: Guard wall down the right side, looking along travel. This is a real barrier, so turning it off lets cargo leave the belt sideways.

params.label: Guard height (m)
params.desc: How far the side guards stand above the conveying surface. Lower them to see and reach a small product, raise them for tall cartons on a fast line. Each conveyor keeps its own height, so two that meet with different heights show a step at the joint. A photo eye mounted on a guard looks across 0.08 m above the surface: over a guard lower than that, through a hole in a taller one.

params.label: Guard openings
params.desc: Gaps cut in the guard wall, measured as distance ALONG the belt from the tail. Side -1 is left, +1 is right, 0 cuts both. Each gap opens the collision as well as the mesh, which is how a transfer or a diverter gets product off the lane.

params.label: Guard holes [s m, y m, side ±1]
params.desc: Where sensor beams cross the side guards. Worked out by the host from the scene; not for editing.

params.label: Guard mitres [x m, c, side ±1]
params.desc: Where a guard end is cut at an angle to meet the guard of the conveyor this one merges with. Worked out by the host from the scene; not for editing.

params.label: Rail cuts [x m, c, side ±1]
params.desc: Where a frame rail end is cut to fit against the frame of the conveyor this one merges onto. Worked out by the host from the scene; not for editing.

params.label: Rail extents [side ±1, back m, front m]
params.desc: Where the rails and guards STOP on each side, in belt-local X. Normally written by the host: when another conveyor merges flush against a side, this retracts the rails to its outer wall instead of running them through its frame. Worked out by the host from the scene; not for editing.

params.label: Support legs
params.desc: Master switch for the leg set below. Off leaves the bed floating, which is what you want when it is carried by a mezzanine or bolted to another frame.

params.label: Leg rests [x0 m, x1 m, dy m]
params.desc: Per-leg floor heights for stretches where the surface underneath is NOT this part own floor plane - a platform deck crossing under, or a drop past it. Host-written at placement; a leg squeezed into less than 5 cm is dropped rather than drawn stubby.

params.label: Tail leg
params.desc: Draw a leg pair at the tail - the upstream end, where cargo arrives.

params.label: Tail inset (m)
params.desc: How far back from the tail drum the end leg stands. Increase it to clear whatever butts up against this end.

params.label: Tail clearance (m)
params.desc: Dead band past the tail leg before the evenly-spaced middle legs are allowed to start.

params.label: Head leg
params.desc: Draw a leg pair at the head - the downstream end, where cargo discharges.

params.label: Head inset (m)
params.desc: How far back from the head drum the end leg stands. Increase it to clear whatever butts up against this end.

params.label: Head clearance (m)
params.desc: Dead band before the head leg that the evenly-spaced middle legs must stop short of.

params.label: Middle legs
params.desc: Fill the span between the end legs with evenly-spaced intermediate ones.

params.label: Middle leg spacing (m)
params.desc: Target gap between intermediate legs: 3.05 m is a real run supported at every 10 ft bed joint. The middle legs step on multiples of it, so the actual gap lands at or just under this.

params.label: Exclusion start (m)
params.desc: Start of a stretch, measured along the belt from the tail, where no leg is drawn - room for a floor conveyor, a pit or a walkway crossing beneath. Leaving start and end equal disables the zone.

params.label: Exclusion end (m)
params.desc: End of the no-leg stretch. It must be GREATER than the start, or the zone is ignored entirely.

params.desc: The program commands belt speed here, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0 - so a half-wired belt sits still rather than running at its authored speed.

params.label: Running tag (true while moving)

params.label: Speed that reads 30 (m/s)
params.desc: The surface speed this conveyor reaches when its drive turns at 30. It scales the velocity tag: running at exactly this speed reads 30.

params.label: Speed that reads 30 (FPM)
params.desc: The surface speed, in feet per minute, this conveyor reaches when its drive turns at 30. It scales the velocity tag: running at exactly this speed reads 30.

params.label: Velocity tag (30 at the speed above)

params.label: Travel per pulse (in)
params.desc: How far the surface travels between pulses on the pulse tag. A pulse cannot be finer than one simulation step, so a fast conveyor at a fine pitch needs a higher project simHz.

params.label: Pulse tag (one per pitch)
params.desc: An encoder for the program to count: TRUE for one simulation step each time the surface has travelled the inches above, in either direction, and FALSE otherwise.

params.desc: Odometer of surface travel in metres, integrated on sim time: it climbs while the conveyor runs forward and counts back while it reverses. signals.name: tag
signals.label: Presence tag
signals.desc: Where the photoeye publishes presence for the program to read. Whether true means blocked or clear is set by Normally closed above.

params.label: Max range (m)
params.desc: How far down the beam a target still counts as present. The beam is cast along local +Z, so aim the sensor by rotating it; snapping it onto a conveyor guard fits this range across the lane for you.

params.label: Sensing mode
params.desc: How the eye is installed. Diffuse: the target itself reflects the light back to the eye, so nothing stands opposite it. Retro-reflective: the eye looks at a reflector on the far side of the lane and a target breaking that beam is detected; the reflector is drawn at Max range, so snapping the eye onto a conveyor guard puts it on the far guard. In the sim both detect the same way: a target in the beam before Max range.

params.label: Show beam
params.desc: Draw the beam line in the viewport. A viewing aid only - hiding it does not change what the sensor detects.

params.label: Normally closed (inverts the signal)
params.desc: Invert the output, so the tag reads true when NOTHING is detected. The beam colour still follows the real detection, not the inverted signal.

params.label: Only marked targets
params.desc: Count a target only if a machine upstream left this mark on it (wrapped, or a label a labeller wrote). Empty: anything in the beam counts. This is how a program checks a product, not just its presence - a load that was never wrapped reads as clear.

params.label: Presence tag
params.desc: Where the photoeye publishes presence for the program to read. Whether true means blocked or clear is set by Normally closed above.

params.label: Length (m)
params.desc: Extent along local X. Drives the collision body as well as the visual, and the box is centred on its origin.

params.label: Width (m)
params.desc: Extent along local Z. Drives the collision body as well as the visual.

params.label: Height (m)
params.desc: Extent along local Y. Drives the collision body as well as the visual.

params.label: Mass (kg)
params.desc: Physical mass. Heavier cargo is harder for a conveyor to accelerate and pushes lighter cargo out of the way.

params.label: Color
params.desc: Tint over the cardboard texture. White leaves it untinted.
